identity.real_world_identity_notes: FIA evidence establishes the S7 competition identity, and specialist technical reporting supports a six-speed sequential transmission in the S7-R family. Exact AMS2 cockpit inspection confirms a sequential stick without paddles.

wheel_rim.notes: Direct cockpit inspection showed a round rim without an integrated display; exact diameter remains unknown.

notes: With Auto Clutch disabled, the car stalled when moving from rest without physical clutch input.
All six sequential-stick gears accepted clutch-free full-throttle upshifts with automatic throttle cut.
Clutch-free downshifts were accepted and no automatic throttle blip was observed; authentic rev matching therefore requires the driver to blip the throttle manually.
The strongest opened transmission source describes a later S7-R, so exact 2005 historical revision details remain qualified.
Live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with Auto Clutch disabled.
Standing-start clutch, six-speed sequential stick without paddles, automatic cut, no automatic blip, and round no-display rim were directly observed.

confidence.basis: Exact simulator identity, modeled hardware, and shift behavior were directly tested; FIA and specialist evidence support the historical car and sequential transmission family while the exact 2005 revision remains qualified.

claims.basis: Official release, homologation context, and exact live CarModel/class observation establish the simulated identity.
Specialist family-level evidence and direct exercise of the modeled six-speed sequential stick agree; the historical source is from a later S7-R.
Direct current-game testing and cockpit inspection establish the start clutch, automatic cut, absence of automatic blip, required manual rev matching, and wheel shape.
